title: Ayikple
localName: Ayikple — bean and toasted corn one-pot
author: Barbara Baeta
desc: Taught at Flair Catering in Accra — adzuki beans simmered an hour with smoked herring and crayfish, then bound with up to two cups of toasted corn flour.
longDesc: Ayikple is beans and toasted corn flour in one pot, and this version was taught by Barbara Baeta at her Flair Catering in Accra — which makes it one of the few recipes in the Ghanaian record traceable to a named professional kitchen. A cup of adzuki beans simmers about an hour with a third of a cup of smoked herring, a quarter cup of dried crayfish, ginger, salt and sliced jalapeño or kpakpo shito. A cup and a third to a cup and a half of tomato gravy goes in, and then up to two cups of toasted corn flour — ablemanu — to bind it. Her warning is specific: do not substitute cornmeal.
ingredients: About 1/4 cup sliced jalapeño, or 6 kpakpo shito
Up to 2 cups toasted corn flour (ablemanu)
steps: Simmer the adzuki beans about 1 hour, until tender.
Add the smoked herring, dried crayfish, salt, ginger and sliced chillies.
Add the toasted corn flour gradually, stirring, until the mixture binds.
Use up to 2 cups of corn flour depending on how stiff you want it.
chefTips: Toasted corn flour — ablemanu — and not cornmeal. Her instruction is explicit: do not substitute corn meal, which is too coarse and gritty.
Add the corn flour gradually. Up to two cups is the ceiling, not the requirement, and how much you need depends on how wet the beans and gravy are.
An hour on the adzuki beans. They need to be properly tender before anything else goes in, because nothing after this stage softens them further.
Smoked herring and dried crayfish together are the savoury base. Neither is optional if you want this to taste like itself.
A quarter cup of sliced jalapeño or six kpakpo shito — the source offers both, and the kpakpo shito is the Ghanaian choice.
The tomato gravy is a separate preparation and is quantified by volume, so make it first — see GHA047.
Toasted corn flour is the same ingredient as the tom brown in aprapransa, and the two dishes share the technique of binding a wet pot with it.
commonMistakes: Using cornmeal instead of toasted corn flour.
Adding all two cups of flour at once.
Beans not fully tender before the rest goes in.
Leaving out either the herring or the crayfish.
Letting it catch — this mixture is thick and scorches easily.
sources: Adapted from 'Recipe #63: Basic tomato gravy and #64 Ayikple', betumiblog.blogspot.com. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Posted by Fran at 3:47 PM', timestamped 2011-06-25. ALL QUANTITIES SINGLE-PASS AND UNVERIFIED — this page was read once only.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 1 cup adzuki beans (8 oz); ⅓ cup smoked herring; ¼ cup dried crayfish; 1 teaspoon salt; 2 teaspoons ginger; about ¼ cup sliced jalapeño, or 6 kpakpo shito; '1⅓–1½ cups tomato gravy'; 'Up to 2 cups toasted corn flour (ablemanu)'. Yield as printed: 4 servings. Beans simmer about 1 hour.
THE WARNING, verbatim: 'Do not substitute corn meal, which is too coarse and "gritty."' Toasted corn flour (ablemanu) is a distinct product and the recipe does not work without it.

THE PROVENANCE, and the reason this entry matters out of proportion to its length: the recipe was TAUGHT BY BARBARA BAETA AT FLAIR CATERING. Baeta is the Ghanaian chef who co-authored The Ghana Cookbook with Fran Osseo-Asare, and Flair Catering is her Accra business. Almost nothing attributable to Baeta is retrievable in print — her co-authored cookbook's quantities sit behind a paywall and no recipe consulted elsewhere is bylined to her — so a dish traceable to her kitchen is unusually valuable. The display author field credits her as the source of the method; the transcription is Osseo-Asare's.
THE CORN FLOUR IS TOASTED, NOT FERMENTED. This dish involves no fermentation and needs no fermentation cue.
THE TOMATO GRAVY it calls for is quantified by volume and published separately at GHA047, from the same post.
NO DONENESS CUE is printed beyond the one-hour bean simmer and the instruction to add flour until bound. The 'binds' language above follows the source's own framing of the corn flour's role.

ON ABLEMANU: toasted corn flour, the same ingredient as the 'tom brown' that thickens aprapransa at GHA010. The two dishes use it the same way — as a binder stirred into a wet pot — which is a technique worth recognising across the cuisine.
storage: 4 days refrigerated. It sets very firm.
reheating: Low heat with water or extra gravy to loosen.
healthBenefits: Adzuki beans are high in plant protein, folate, iron and soluble fibre.
Smoked herring and dried crayfish both supply protein, calcium and iodine.
Toasted maize adds fibre and B vitamins.
A complete one-pot meal with legume and cereal protein combined.
culturalNote: Binding a pot of beans with toasted corn flour is the same move that makes aprapransa, and it belongs to a family of West African one-pots that turn a stew into a meal without a separate starch. That this one comes down through a named Accra caterer rather than a village kitchen is a reminder that professional Ghanaian cooking has its own transmission line.
